title: BARNETT DBAP -- two sources panned over the 8-speaker Barnett Hall rig

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Turn on DSP (OUTPUT). Speaker N plays on interface output N.
Source A is mono, source B is stereo. Each picks File, Live (adc ch) or Inlet in its SOURCE menu.
File: drop an audio file or click open, then play (and loop). trim sets the input level.
Drag the puck on the plan to place the source. src Z (m) sets its height.
rolloff, blur: how sharply level falls off with distance, and how much it spreads.
width, decorr: spread the source into two points and blur them apart.
air: distance high-cut. hull: dB/m of fade when the source moves outside the speaker ring.
WEIGHTS favour or mute speakers. TRIMS (dB) offset each speaker. MASTER sets the output level.
SCENES: pick a slot number, then store or recall. read / write save the slots to disk.
MOTION -> A: switch on, pick a path (orbit ... spiral, recorded) and shape it with the dials.
rec: draw a gesture with the puck to make the recorded path. loop menu + cue fire one-shots.
wander adds drift on top of any path. Motion settings are stored in source A's scenes.
VERIFY PING: pick a speaker number and click to send a noise burst to that speaker only.
VENUE read: load another venue layout (JSON) with speaker positions and alignment delays.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: Each source is a dbap-source bpatcher (args: name, 1 = mono / 2 = stereo) with its own js dbap.js.
The js solves Distance-Based Amplitude Panning over the hall's speaker layout into 8 gains.
The gains ramp an 8-channel mc signal. Both sources sum through alignment delays to mc.dac~ 1-8.
Both modules also accept '<control> <value>' messages to set any control (see control-demo).
